hyperedges.label: Running-set selection
hyperedges.description: active.ts names the deliberately narrow running set; cases.ts#loadCases filters the frozen prospects pool down to exactly those ids, refusing to run silently fewer cases than declared.

hyperedges.label: Blind judging pipeline
hyperedges.description: judgeRun tops up cached readings via judgeOnce (a no-tools, blinded model call), and judgementFrom/consensus fold multiple readings into one grade per axis (correctness, similarity) with an agreement figure — never a single unverified opinion.

hyperedges.label: Index lifecycle and continuity model
hyperedges.description: An Index describes one Snapshot; Capture copies a finished Index into a Baseline for later comparison; Continuity later resolves a subject across Snapshots/Baselines without ever mutating the live Index.

hyperedges.label: pre-run setup pipeline
hyperedges.description: The three things that must happen before a bench run spends any quota: preflight refuses cases whose declared base commit would void their ground truth, prewarm builds and caches the codedocs index for every commit the surviving cases need, and buildPrompt assembles the task each arm is actually given — all three operate on the same BenchCase[] before any agent is spawned.

hyperedges.label: quota-free reconstruction pipeline
hyperedges.description: recordFrom is a pure fold from a run's saved stream/patch to a RunRecord; rescore.ts replays it over every saved run on disk when scoring logic changes, and rejudge.ts fills in judgements for records rescore left alone — together they let bench/report.ts's numbers be corrected after the fact without re-running the agent.

hyperedges.label: graduated difficulty corpus
hyperedges.description: The prospect pool is built to span the difficulty scale end to end: 333230 is the level-1 control where the file is already named on eight stack frames, 332885 is a level-3 case whose answer crosses two layers joined only through an interface, and 329074 is the level-4 case with the pool's furthest symptom-to-cause distance — together they let bench/report.ts's level grouping show whether codedocs' benefit actually grows with structural distance.

hyperedges.label: single-run pipeline
hyperedges.description: One (case, arm, replicate) cell flows through worktree execution, stream parsing into metrics, diff scoring against ground truth, and judge grading before being filed as a RunRecord — the full measurement pipeline for one benchmark run.

hyperedges.label: blinded two-axis judging
hyperedges.description: The judge is deliberately shown only issue/fix/patch (no arm identity) and graded on two independent axes — correctness and similarity to the maintainers' fix — so resemblance cannot masquerade as correctness.

hyperedges.label: difficulty ladder
hyperedges.description: Four case levels form a structural-complexity ladder from 'report names the file' (level 1, the control) to 'cause is a relationship over time with no identifier' (level 4), testing the claim that codedocs' benefit grows with complexity.

hyperedges.label: The `docs draft` ADR triangle
hyperedges.description: ADR 0013 reverses ADR 0006's deletion of `docs generate` by answering the coverage-inversion objection ADR 0005's claim model raises, via the `codedocs?:` candidate marker; the three ADRs jointly define what `docs draft` may write and why a draft is not a document.

hyperedges.label: Draft write-and-refuse flow
hyperedges.description: main.ts#drafted resolves the target path and calls draft-out.ts#writeDraft; a refusal (draft-exists / draft-unwritable) is rendered back to the user via messages.ts#formatError while the computed draft still reaches stdout, so nothing is lost by the refusal.

hyperedges.label: Benchmark write-up assembly
hyperedges.description: writeup.ts#build composes the prose functions from writeup-prose.ts (question, provenance, standing, limits, colophon) with the tables from writeup-tables.ts into the single generated RESULTS.md, so no number or caveat in the document can exist without a corresponding record on disk.

hyperedges.label: docs draft assembly pipeline
hyperedges.description: draft() owns section selection and bounding; it reads facts through the same assembleEvidence/fileReport an `evidence`/`file` answer uses, shapes them into fact groups via draft-facts.ts, and hands the whole to draft-markdown.ts#markdownFor for byte-identical rendering. Each stage owns one concern: subject resolution, fact assembly, fact-to-line rendering, and file-to-Markdown rendering.

hyperedges.label: candidate/claim consistency guarantee
hyperedges.description: ADR 0013's core promise — a draft cannot disagree with an evidence answer about the same subject — rests on symbolBody and fileBody both calling the same claimsFor() over the same report shapes that evidence() calls it over, rather than each implementing its own restatement.

hyperedges.label: draft file safety contract
hyperedges.description: The manifest declares --out with no --force; the envelope's closed error set enforces refusal to overwrite (draft-exists) and surfaces write failures (draft-unwritable); the candidate marker ensures the file that could be overwritten is never mistaken for a checked document.

nodes.label: Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Stored with the facts it describes and never recomputed at query time, because it reports the analysis that ran rather than the machine as it is now. A property of a file, never of the repository, and never a claim about completeness. A three-valued typed/partial/syntactic enum was rejected because it folds completeness into fidelity and the two invalidate on different triggers.

nodes.label: Precondition
nodes.rationale: An unmet precondition lowers fidelity; it is not an error. Refusal would imply a repo-wide verdict, and one unprepared package in a 34-project monorepo must not downgrade the other 33.

nodes.label: Remediation
nodes.rationale: codedocs reports remediations and never runs them, and never guesses one: postinstall is arbitrary code from a possibly unfamiliar repository, and the capability gains nothing because the caller can already run commands with the user's consent.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.rationale: Carried by the fact itself rather than attached when rendering, and per edge instance rather than per edge kind, because the same edge kind is deterministic at one call site and inferred at the next — getSignatureUsage reports both call sites for all three declarations of an interface plus its implementations.

nodes.label: Blind spot
nodes.rationale: Named concretely and per answer, never summarised as a score: '40% of imports unresolved' cannot tell a caller whether this answer is affected, and any threshold built on it is indefensible.

nodes.label: Completeness
nodes.rationale: A property of one answer, not of the index: an answer is complete or it names its blind spots. Kept apart from fidelity because the two invalidate on different triggers.

nodes.label: Preflight
nodes.rationale: Split in two because only signals 1-3 can run before a program is open; they cost microseconds so they run unconditionally, and the fourth signal is a by-product of extraction rather than a pass of its own. A type checker's diagnostics are not a signal: they cost 3,100x the specifier scan and cannot tell a prepared repository from an unprepared one.

nodes.label: Environment fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Joins the cache key per project, because analysing a fresh clone and then running install leaves no file content changed, so an incremental pass would serve the syntactic answer forever — confidently wrong by caching. Declaration files alone are hashed because a new source file is drift the wave already repairs, while nothing imports a declaration file. None of the inputs walks node_modules, which is the accepted blind spot doctor --measure exists for.

nodes.label: Unresolved specifier
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a fact with its cause rather than dropped, and never as a ratio. Reported deduplicated because one absent generated artefact produced 302 of them on cal.com. unmapped and broken get no remediation — none would help the first and none is a command for the second.

nodes.label: codedocs.jsonc configuration
nodes.rationale: Holds only the facts codedocs cannot determine and must be told; anything it can determine is not a fact it needs telling, so preferences are excluded by construction. Strict because an unrecognised key is a typo — `exlucde` parsing to nothing silently is the failure this buys out. No key may change what is reported about what was analysed.

nodes.label: Node (five node types)
nodes.rationale: Repository is the index header rather than a node: with containment derived from the SymbolId it is the source and target of no edges, and a node with no edges is a header wearing a costume.

nodes.label: Edge (nine edge kinds)
nodes.rationale: A closed enum, so adding a variant forces the question 'which backend actually produces this?'. calls and references stay separate kinds because SCIP's conflation of them was the defect that ruled it out as the producer. contains edges are not stored, because containment is already encoded in the SymbolId.

nodes.label: SymbolId
nodes.rationale: Two normalisations: the workspace package version is a fixed placeholder, because a routine version bump would otherwise invalidate every symbol in a package; and locals are named by descriptor path rather than ordinal. (path, offset) was rejected because adding a newline would churn every symbol in a file. The file is one backtick-escaped namespace descriptor rather than one per path segment, because the segmented form cannot be parsed.

nodes.label: Descriptor path
nodes.rationale: Each segment is taken from what the author wrote, which is what makes an id survive a sibling being inserted above it where an ordinal does not. Anonymous callbacks contribute the call they are an argument to, including its first string literal, because naming only declarations collapsed 6,746 of cal.com's declarations onto 1,571 ids. Segments are capped at 96 characters, costing 31 collisions out of 48,517.

nodes.label: Collision
nodes.rationale: Reported, never merged silently, because the answer really is their union: an over-report that names itself is wrong in a way an over-report presented as complete is not. 405 declarations across 330 ids on cal.com, none on the Next fixture. No durable id collides.

nodes.label: Durable
nodes.rationale: Local symbols are not durable and nothing durable may anchor to one. Locals are still indexed rather than excluded, because 25 of the Next fixture's 175 call edges are calls to local bindings — 14% of a call graph is not an edge case.

nodes.label: Derivation
nodes.rationale: 'This edge is inferred' is not actionable; 'inferred because it was matched by shared method name across implementations' is. Named derivation rather than method because method already means a class member here.

nodes.label: Continuity
nodes.rationale: A separate inferred layer that may never touch the SymbolId, because no existing system has managed to make identity survive a rename, and every surveyed system correctly refused to put a heuristic inside a primary key.

nodes.label: Candidate
nodes.rationale: Ranked by evidence rather than by a score, and never asserted as the answer even when alone in the list — the same fixture produced two candidates for one name. An empty list means no candidate was found, never that the subject was deleted.

nodes.label: Label
nodes.rationale: A third kind of thing beside nodes and edges, never a sixth node type: a Label node's entire existence would be one edge back to its subject. Keyed by node id, so it labels a Symbol as readily as a File, which is what makes the deferred component/hook layer additive.

nodes.label: Role axis (source / test / config)
nodes.rationale: Test helpers, mocks and fixtures fold into `test` because everything that excludes tests wants them excluded too, and a second role means every caller must remember to name both. Mostly inferred, because nothing but convention knows what a test is; runner configs are TypeScript whose globs exist only after evaluation, and codedocs never executes repository code.

nodes.label: Authorship axis (authored / generated)
nodes.rationale: Orthogonal to role, because generated code is still source and a config file is still authored. Mostly deterministic, because git knows what it does not track.

nodes.label: Package node
nodes.rationale: External packages are nodes, named but not walked; external symbols are never materialised, because cal.com's sweep left 92,673 call sites crossing into node_modules against 26,091 resolved in-repo.

nodes.label: Project node
nodes.rationale: Not in the PRD and not a Package: cal.com has 34 tsconfigs and no root config. A file may belong to several projects, one of which is canonical, so analysedIn is stored where containment is not.

nodes.label: Export-shape hash
nodes.rationale: Gates incremental propagation: a file whose content changed but whose export shape did not stops the wave, so a body-only edit — the commonest edit there is — settles in one round and one file.

nodes.label: Shape hash
nodes.rationale: Computed from typeToString and structural expansion, never from Type.id, which was measured turning a body-only edit into 10 waves and 1,436 of 3,000 files because type ids are assigned lazily per snapshot.

nodes.label: Caller attribution
nodes.rationale: The walk seeks the nearest callable ancestor first, not the nearest named one: stopping at the nearest named declaration credits a hook's calls to the constant holding its result, so callees on any hook returns nothing and the call graph fragments into single-edge islands. Module-level and anonymous-callback calls are attributed to the file — the honest answer, not a dropped edge.

nodes.label: Unresolved call
nodes.rationale: Stored as a fact with its cause rather than dropped. `dynamic` must be recorded even though there is nothing to point at, because it is the one cause where codedocs cannot know what it missed.

nodes.label: Index
nodes.rationale: A derived artifact: never committed, always safe to delete. Committing it was measured, not assumed — six commits of about a hundred rows grew .git by 25MB because binary files do not delta, and two branches that both re-analysed would conflict in a file no one can merge by hand.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: One index holds exactly one snapshot, which is what makes a SymbolId snapshot-scoped. A snapshot column on every table was rejected: it taxes every query and write when a separate 20MB file copies in 9ms and evicts by deleting.

nodes.label: Index header
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing part of every honest answer, and what it means to demote Repository from a node to a header. Stores the paths the last tree walk saw as well as the analysed set, because drift is decided against the previous walk.

nodes.label: Drift
nodes.rationale: Detected before every answer and either repaired or named. A file counts as new against the previous tree walk rather than against the analysed set, because otherwise every source file no tsconfig globs reads as newly appeared on every query forever — 519 of them in this repo. Branch switch, rebase and a dirty tree need no special cases: they are all just files whose signature changed.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.rationale: Recorded by capture rather than built on demand, because a git worktree of an old commit has no node_modules and codedocs will not run an install, so every file in a reconstructed baseline would be syntactic. Three are kept, evicting non-ancestors of HEAD first — which is the whole branch-switching story.

nodes.label: Document
nodes.rationale: Found by scanning for claims rather than by a docs/** convention: cal.com has zero Markdown under docs/ and 55 READMEs beside the code they describe, plus changelogs and licences that must never be checked. Writing a claim is how a file opts in — a 9ms scan needing no configuration.

nodes.label: Claim
nodes.rationale: Written beside the prose it justifies, in an HTML comment invisible on GitHub and plain text in a diff, so a contradicted section can be reported rather than a contradicted file. Frontmatter was rejected because the list and the prose drift apart silently. A closed predicate set, for the reason the edge enum is closed.

nodes.label: Verdict
nodes.rationale: Each of the four has exactly one producer and nothing blends them; provenance is reported alongside a verdict, never as a fifth one, because eight states would be a switch nobody acts on differently. contradicted requires a claim to be falsified, never merely unresolved: 12 of 20 then 95 of 105 vanished ids were moves.

nodes.label: Claim coverage
nodes.rationale: Reported with every verdict so `verified` cannot be read as 'all of this is true'. It counts sections and says nothing about whether the prose in them is right; it is never combined with completeness into a score.

nodes.label: Operation
nodes.rationale: The unit the whole product is built from. Nothing composes operations above them, because a composing binding would be a second product surface to keep correct and the CLI, --json and MCP would drift apart.

nodes.label: Renderer
nodes.rationale: A pure function of the envelope: it may group, colour and page, never re-sort or withhold silently. --limit's default belongs here rather than to the operation, so a terminal gets 20 while --json is unbounded.

nodes.label: Envelope
nodes.rationale: One shape for success and failure alike, so a parser never meets a second shape. conditions are scoped to only the projects the answer touched, which stops the envelope growing with the size of the repository rather than the size of the question. An error is a code and typed parameters, never a formatted sentence, which is what lets report-bug carry the code and drop the parameters.

nodes.label: Report (report-bug artefact)
nodes.rationale: Split by reader rather than by sensitivity: the default carries facts about codedocs and the machine alone so it is safe to paste in public unread, and --with-repository is the opt-in. The only artefact meant to leave the machine, and codedocs writes it but never moves it.

nodes.label: Truncation
nodes.rationale: Distinct from a blind spot because codedocs knows exactly what it withheld. --json is unbounded by default: a capped answer an agent does not know is capped is a wrong answer with a footnote.

nodes.label: Scope
nodes.rationale: Reported as an excluded count rather than a blind spot, because filing a known exclusion as a blind spot teaches readers that blind spots are routine, which would destroy the signal. Expressed as one generic label pair rather than bespoke flags like --no-tests.

nodes.label: codedocs mcp server
nodes.rationale: Not an operation but a server that binds them: one tool per operation, same name, same arguments, returning the machine envelope verbatim, and no tool that is not an operation. Without that rule written down the server grows convenience tools and 'thin wrapper' quietly becomes false.

nodes.label: codedocs / fallow boundary
nodes.rationale: codedocs implements no analysis fallow already ships — not because the overlap would be hard, but because two tools answering one question about one repository will disagree and you would have no way to decide which is right. The question's shape decides the tool.

nodes.label: @codedocs/core package
nodes.rationale: Private and never published; exposes one flat surface of one exported function per operation, so nothing in the binding can compose two of them.

nodes.label: @codedocs/cli package
nodes.rationale: The only public surface, bundled by tsdown into one ESM file with core bundled in rather than published, because Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules so a build is forced.

nodes.label: openSession
nodes.rationale: The one door to the index. Config is read before the store is opened, because a config that cannot be used means the user's intent is unknown. Four senses of out-of-date are kept apart because they are repaired differently.

nodes.label: Propagation wave repair
nodes.rationale: Propagates to direct importers only where an export-shape hash moved. A ceiling of eight waves turns a bug in the shape hash into a slow answer rather than a hung process, falling back to a cold build that analyse reports.

nodes.label: Cold build, committed per project
nodes.rationale: Committing per project is a correctness choice, not a performance one: against 22.9s all commit granularities are noise, and per project is the grain fidelity and analysis conditions are already held at, so a half-built index is expressible in the existing vocabulary.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 adapter (adapter/ts7)
nodes.rationale: The only module that knows a TypeScript backend exists. The contract is array-first — 'give me facts for these N files', never per symbol — because batching is a 17x effect that cannot be retrofitted, and it is the seam that makes the bet on an explicitly unstable API reversible. The boundary is specified as the facts the adapter owes, because the leaks that hurt are semantic, not typed.

nodes.label: Operation manifest
nodes.rationale: The operation set held as data, from which the CLI parser, --help, the MCP tool list, the JSON schema and the reference docs are all derived — so an operation that reaches one binding and misses another fails to build. The only mechanism that makes the renderer contract enforceable rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: String interning in the store
nodes.rationale: A SymbolId names a file plus its descriptors, so storing it verbatim wrote each path several times per symbol and twice more per edge. Invisible above the store module, and it takes cal.com's index from 61MB to 17.6MB.

nodes.label: Stat-signature drift detection
nodes.rationale: Git is deliberately absent: git status costs ~90ms, cannot see untracked and ignored files a tsconfig still globs, and collapses in a checkout that is not a repository. Hashing everything costs 280ms to learn what 17ms of stat already says, so only flagged files are hashed.

nodes.label: Labels and scope module
nodes.rationale: Recomputed whole whenever the index is repaired, never invalidated file by file — 156 files in 13ms in this repository, which is what makes the simple rule affordable. Every signal that fires is stored with its own provenance; precedence decides only which one an answer acts on, which is what lets doctor report disagreements.

nodes.label: Four generic preflight signals
nodes.rationale: Generic rather than a framework registry, so an unknown framework degrades correctly; a framework lookup only turns a fired signal into a concrete remediation string and is allowed to be absent. Signal 3 is load-bearing: a full successful install cleared every unprepared cause yet left redwood with no .redwood/ and next with no next-env.d.ts — framework codegen is not an install step.

nodes.label: SCIP symbol string in a codedocs scheme
nodes.rationale: SCIP is an open, versioned, vendor-neutral grammar that already solves cross-package naming, and Meta stores SCIP strings verbatim. It is rejected as a storage substrate on its authors' own terms — efficient navigation is an explicit non-goal — so the naming scheme and the store are two decisions, not one.
nodes.norm_label: scip symbol string in a codedocs scheme

nodes.label: Five node types
nodes.rationale: Three of the PRD's seven boxes do not survive: Relationship is the edge set not a sibling of File, Change is git's job, and Repository is the index header.

nodes.label: Nine edge kinds, closed enum
nodes.rationale: Kythe's open (source, kind, target) triple was rejected because it pushes all schema into convention, and the deterministic/inferred distinction needs exhaustiveness to be checkable.

nodes.label: Two orthogonal classification axes
nodes.rationale: linguist-js was rejected on measurement: its two headline signals classify 13 of 5,207 TypeScript files across three fixtures. A fixture role, a vendored role and a declaration role were each rejected on measurement too — the declaration role would misclassify 35 real files to catch none.

nodes.label: node:sqlite as the index store
nodes.rationale: node:sqlite rather than better-sqlite3 because it ships inside Node 24.19 with no native module built at install time on a toolchain we do not control, and SQLite is public domain so no redistribution audit reapplies. This is not a decision to use SQLite's query engine — a warm 'who calls X' is 0.04us from a plain Map; load time, memory and partial writes were the problem.

nodes.label: Stat signature, not git, decides staleness
nodes.rationale: Under 120ms buys a complete answer to 'which files moved' without git, which cannot see untracked or ignored files a Project still globs — 183 of them on the fixtures — and which the index must work without entirely.
nodes.norm_label: stat signature, not git, decides staleness

nodes.label: Discard the index on a version mismatch, never migrate
nodes.rationale: A migration is a maintenance burden on every schema change whose failure mode is a subtly wrong index nobody can detect, priced against a 22.9s rebuild whose failure mode is a wait. TypeScript's own builder does exactly this.
nodes.norm_label: discard the index on a version mismatch, never migrate

nodes.label: Closed predicate set for claims
nodes.rationale: A query language was rejected for the reason SQL was kept out of the CLI: it becomes an interface that cannot change, and every unparseable query becomes a support case. Negation and counts matter most, because counts catch the fourth implementation being added, which no per-instance claim ever will. analysedIn is deliberately not exposed: it asserts something about codedocs, not about the repository.

nodes.label: Pointers cannot decide staleness (measurement)
nodes.rationale: File pointers false-alarm at 71.2% and directory pointers at 77.1%, and miss 47% of real breakage at 60 commits because symbols break without their own file being touched. All 500 of cal.com's last 500 commits touch one package, so a pointer written there fires forever and means nothing.

nodes.label: Three bindings, one to one with the operation set
nodes.rationale: --json is explicit and never inferred from a TTY, because sniffing a pipe makes the same command produce different output depending on where it runs — which an agent capturing output through a pty discovers the hard way.
nodes.norm_label: three bindings, one to one with the operation set

nodes.label: Three channels of honesty that must not blur
nodes.rationale: Refines ADR 0003: a scope exclusion is an excluded count beside the echoed scope, not a blind spot, because codedocs knows precisely what it withheld and filing a known exclusion as a blind spot teaches readers that blind spots are routine.
nodes.norm_label: three channels of honesty that must not blur

nodes.label: No-network invariant
nodes.rationale: Two gates hold it: oxlint's no-restricted-imports/globals over first-party source, and pnpm check:network over the production dependency closure. A demonstrably local socket is added as a named ALLOWED row naming the package, the one module and the reason — never by widening the module list.

nodes.label: Localization benchmark
nodes.rationale: Localization is chosen over fixing because a fix has many valid shapes and would need a judge model, while localization has one true answer written by the maintainers — isolating the cost of navigating an unfamiliar codebase, which is the thing codedocs claims to change.

nodes.label: Benchmark baseline arm
nodes.rationale: Keeps Bash, because grep and find are how anyone searches a repository from a shell and removing it would rig the result. A run where the baseline reaches for codedocs anyway is thrown out and counted, not silently included.

nodes.label: Benchmark codedocs arm
nodes.rationale: The ~150-token briefing is charged to this arm on every turn, because that is the real cost of putting a tool in front of an agent and hiding it would flatter the tool. Runs at syntactic fidelity, so the result is a floor: typed fidelity can add edges, not remove them.

nodes.label: Benchmark metrics (tokens, calls, files, sec, hit, sym)
nodes.rationale: Cache reads count because a cached token is still a token the model read. Files opened is counted conservatively so the bias always runs against the tool being sold. Medians not means, because with three replicates one runaway loop would drag a mean somewhere no typical run goes.
nodes.norm_label: benchmark metrics (tokens, calls, files, sec, hit, sym)

nodes.label: Changesets release flow
nodes.rationale: Uses a PAT rather than GITHUB_TOKEN so the version PR triggers CI — a branch pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN raises no pull_request event. Runs version-packages rather than a bare changeset version, because changeset version writes package.json only and the lockfile would report the previous version forever. Secrets are asserted up front because an empty org secret resolves to an empty string rather than failing.

nodes.label: npm provenance publishing
nodes.rationale: Signs the published tarball with the run's identity so a reader can tie the registry package back to the commit; needs id-token: write, and a registry-url matching what changeset publish targets or the publish goes out unauthenticated.

nodes.label: First published release of @codedocs/cli
nodes.rationale: @codedocs/core is bundled in rather than published because Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules, so a build is forced and the CLI is the only public surface. typescript is pinned to an exact 7.0.2 because the adapter uses its explicitly unstable API.

nodes.label: Continuity as a separate inferred layer
nodes.rationale: Recognising that a symbol today is last week's symbol never touches the SymbolId, because no surveyed system can bake a heuristic into a primary key. It is built as two matchers with a ranked candidate list, never a score.
nodes.norm_label: continuity as a separate inferred layer

nodes.label: Subject matching
nodes.rationale: Starts from a Claim subject that no longer resolves, needs no Baseline, and ships with `docs check`. Cannot see a symbol renamed inside a file that never moved unless its name survives.

nodes.label: Snapshot matching
nodes.rationale: Compares two Indexes, needs a Baseline, and waits for `impact`. Presenting it as one degrading interface with subject matching would hide that shape-hash is missing rather than weak.

nodes.label: Two-step git rename probe
nodes.rationale: Find the commit that deleted the path (14 ms on cal.com), then ask that one commit what it did (153 ms). Returns the destination and git's own similarity with no stored state; `git log --follow` costs 465 ms and answers a different question.

nodes.label: Derivation precedence ranking
nodes.rationale: Ordering the derivations strongest-first IS the ranking rule; ranking is lexicographic over the derivation set, falling through to how many fired and finally to SymbolId lexically so the order is total.

nodes.label: content-hash derivation
nodes.rationale: Leads the precedence because identical bytes involve no heuristic at all, and 46% of cal.com's renames are byte-identical. It is also the sole bridge for an unstaged move git cannot pair.

nodes.label: path-prefix-rewrite derivation
nodes.rationale: Outranks git-rename because it is a git rename plus 595 siblings agreeing with it. 94% of renamed files move alongside a sibling, so a directory sweep is one fact rather than 596 coincidences.

nodes.label: name-in-head derivation
nodes.rationale: One-sided and the weakest derivation, kept distinct from declared-name so the weaker cannot inherit the stronger's rank. Never suppressed by a candidate-count threshold, since suppression turns a partial answer into silence.

nodes.label: Ranked candidate list
nodes.rationale: One output shape for both matchers: zero to n Candidates carrying derivations, destination and commit. An empty list means 'no candidate found', never 'deleted', because an absence with no candidate is indistinguishable from an unseen move.

nodes.label: No confidence score, every signal boolean
nodes.rationale: Any signal producing a continuous value forces a threshold, and a threshold is a score wearing a different hat. codedocs inherits exactly one threshold — git's own -M default — and names whose it is.
nodes.norm_label: no confidence score, every signal boolean

nodes.label: Baseline captured by normal use
nodes.rationale: A baseline exists only because codedocs analysed that commit while it was the working tree. There is no `baseline save`: an explicit save asks the user to predict a week in advance which commit they will want to compare against.

nodes.label: Rebuilding a baseline is impossible at usable fidelity
nodes.rationale: A `git worktree add --detach` of cal.com at HEAD~60 takes 1.71 s but produces a tree with no node_modules, and codedocs may not run the install — so every file is syntactic, diffed against a typed working tree. The cost is not 22.9 s, it is 22.9 s of the wrong answer.
nodes.norm_label: rebuilding a baseline is impossible at usable fidelity

nodes.label: Retention: three baselines, count not bytes
nodes.rationale: The unit is a count because capture is per clean-tree analyse, denominated in the user's work sessions; a disk or age budget lets repo velocity (cal.com swings 24x) decide the policy. Three is stated as a guess, with doctor as the place the evidence accrues.
nodes.norm_label: retention: three baselines, count not bytes

nodes.label: Baseline resolution and substitution
nodes.rationale: The newest stored baseline that is an ancestor of HEAD, seeded from the merge base. Using an older ancestor is substitution and is reported through the scope channel — never as a blind spot — carrying requested commit, used commit and distance.

nodes.label: Fidelity change is never a finding
nodes.rationale: A file that was syntactic then and is typed now has not changed; the analysis has. Such files are excluded per project and reported as blind spots naming the cause.
nodes.norm_label: fidelity change is never a finding

nodes.label: Baselines never leave the machine
nodes.rationale: Paths would survive but the environment fingerprint would not, so an imported baseline is 20 MB fetched to answer nothing; and NodeHandle.path case-normalisation makes a macOS-built index disagree with a Linux-built one in a way that reads as a move.

nodes.label: getSemanticDiagnostics leaves the design
nodes.rationale: It was 36.4 s of the 36.4 s preflight cost, is not one of ADR 0001's four signals, and cannot discriminate: Redwood's codegen moved unresolved specifiers 63% while semantic errors moved 7%, and a healthy cal.com carries 17,464. There is nothing to scope.

nodes.label: Signal 4 as per-specifier boolean facts
nodes.rationale: The unresolved-specifier ratio is withdrawn: a rate cannot tell a caller whether this answer is affected, and a continuous signal forces a threshold. Facts are grouped by cause, since 302 of apps/web's 542 are one specifier.

nodes.label: The `unmapped` cause
nodes.rationale: Added because 222 bare `app/…` specifiers resolve under the framework's own resolution and not the declared tsconfig; under three causes codedocs would accuse a working repository of 222 defects. It carries no remediation because a remediation is a command and none exists.

nodes.label: Environment fingerprint, made computable
nodes.rationale: Five inputs: signals 1 and 2, the lockfile hash, compilerOptions, whether the config globs anything, and the set-hash of declaration files. Signals 1-2 are required or an install over a fresh clone reads identically; only declaration files are hashed because the wave cannot repair a file nothing imports.

nodes.label: `doctor --measure` re-runs signals 1-3
nodes.rationale: It reports where the working tree disagrees with what the index stored, opening no program and extracting nothing, because a diagnostic flag that costs a cold build is a hidden `analyse`. doctor exits 1 iff a cause with a remediation is unmet, deduplicating causes across signals.

nodes.label: The rule for entry into codedocs.jsonc
nodes.rationale: Three tests — undetectable, defaulted, scope-only. The corollary keeps the file small: it holds facts, never preferences, so a default --limit, an output format or a colour setting may never enter.
nodes.norm_label: the rule for entry into codedocs.jsonc

nodes.label: `discover` key
nodes.rationale: Both halves are additive: projects add to what the tsconfig walk found, skip adds to SKIP_DIRS which a user cannot subtract from, because a config key appearing to control something hard-coded elsewhere is a config that lies. Neither decides membership.

nodes.label: `remediations` key
nodes.rationale: An ordered array, first match wins, consulted for missing-generated alone, because framework codegen is not an install step and no script codedocs can read names `yarn rw g types`. There is no built-in framework table: a shipped table would be inferred and would rot.

nodes.label: The repository root is the nearest enclosing .git
nodes.rationale: findRepositoryRoot preferring the nearest package.json makes a monorepo package read as its own repository with its own index. package.json survives only where there is no .git. A second codedocs.jsonc below the root is an error naming both paths, not a merge.
nodes.norm_label: the repository root is the nearest enclosing .git

nodes.label: Strict parsing and unknown keys
nodes.rationale: Absent is normal; malformed is exit 2 with no fallback to defaults; unknown keys are an error naming a near neighbour. The evidence is `exclude` arriving with two letters transposed — under lenient parsing it parses, excludes nothing, and never says so.

nodes.label: Alias map rejected
nodes.rationale: It does not change scope; it manufactures edges from a user's guess, and a wrong map produces confidently wrong call edges codedocs cannot detect. unmapped is a stated limit of codedocs, and a knob whose effect is to make that limit invisible is what the file must not contain.

nodes.label: The Report and its default shape
nodes.rationale: report-bug is the only operation whose output is meant to travel. A fact about codedocs or the machine is in the default; a fact naming the user's code is behind --with-repository. The design assumption is that the file is pasted into a public issue unread.
nodes.norm_label: the report and its default shape

nodes.label: Split by reader, not by sensitivity
nodes.rationale: The two readers want opposite things: an agent on the user's machine can already read the source it is being protected from, while a public issue has nothing but the file. One flag whose name says what it adds makes the wrong default recoverable and the right one free.
nodes.norm_label: split by reader, not by sensitivity

nodes.label: EnvelopeError as code plus typed params
nodes.rationale: Free text is the hole no field rule closes — an error message interpolates user input and a SymbolId. Codes and typed params make the classification structural and stay true as errors are added, which a scrubbing regex does not.
nodes.norm_label: envelopeerror as code plus typed params

nodes.label: Hashing paths and SymbolIds rejected
nodes.rationale: A SymbolId is deterministic, not anonymous, so hashing destroys content rather than revealing structure. The two identity defects filed here were found by reading descriptor paths; and a dictionary of filenames is not a hard preimage. Decide which facts go in, never how to disguise them.

nodes.label: No network, checked at build time
nodes.rationale: Writing bytes is where codedocs stops: no upload, no gh issue create, no telemetry. Recorded as an invariant with a test over the dependency tree, because it is worth nothing as prose the moment someone adds an HTTP client for an unrelated reason.
nodes.norm_label: no network, checked at build time

nodes.label: The reader is a developer
nodes.rationale: An agent is one more caller of the same operations, not the reader they are shaped for; `evidence` is one operation among thirteen. The four questions codedocs is for are named against what fails at them today, not against an audience.

nodes.label: The fallow boundary
nodes.rationale: codedocs implements no analysis fallow already ships. Two tools reporting on one repository will disagree and a developer holding two dead-code reports has no way to decide which is right — the second answer costs more than it adds, whichever is more accurate.

nodes.label: `impact` is the only composed operation
nodes.rationale: It needs the continuity matcher against a baseline and then the reachability walk, and no combination of the other operations produces it — the test ADR 0006 set for composition living inside an operation.

nodes.label: `review` and `plan` deleted
nodes.rationale: review is fallow's boundary checks plus impact and docs affected printed together, which is a renderer's job; plan is a ranking, and an inferred ordering cannot also be the determinism guarantee — the same reasoning that deleted `search`.

nodes.label: The build order for the rest
nodes.rationale: Reordered by what a developer can use rather than by what an agent needed: references and file, doctor, the label layer, impact, evidence, docs check and docs affected, report-bug. Each step is gated by the one above it.
nodes.norm_label: the build order for the rest

nodes.label: When an agent should reach for codedocs
nodes.rationale: The goal is not to replace reading source but to stop rediscovering deterministic structure through repeated search. Read the source instead for prose, string search, dynamic dispatch, or anything codedocs reports as a blind spot.
nodes.norm_label: when an agent should reach for codedocs

nodes.label: Choosing the smallest tool
nodes.rationale: `evidence` is usually the right first call because it returns every kind of fact at once; `impact` takes no subject and reads the change from the diff; `trace` is the expensive one and should be bounded with depth.

nodes.label: Reading the envelope honestly
nodes.rationale: blindSpots, budget, request and conditions say how much to trust an answer. A blind spot is what codedocs could not see, truncation is what it withheld knowingly, scope is what the caller excluded — and a missing relationship is not proof that none exists.

nodes.label: GitHub issue tracker conventions
nodes.rationale: Issues and PRDs live as GitHub issues on magicspon/codedocs, managed through the gh CLI, with the repo inferred from git remote.

nodes.label: Wayfinder concepts on GitHub
nodes.rationale: Map is an issue labelled wayfinder:map, tickets are sub-issues, blocking uses GitHub's native dependencies. Both sub-issue and dependency APIs take the database id and need `gh api -F`, since `-f` fails with a 422.

nodes.label: Research findings go to docs/research/
nodes.rationale: Throwaway research branches are rejected because parallel research agents share one working tree and cannot each check out a branch; findings go to a distinct file under docs/research/ on the current branch, linked from the resolution comment.

nodes.label: Single-context domain docs
nodes.rationale: One CONTEXT.md and one docs/adr/ at the root; a CONTEXT-MAP.md would signal a multi-context repo whose per-context docs follow the pnpm workspace roots. Absent files are proceeded past silently, because the producer skill creates them lazily.

nodes.label: The call-site sweep algorithm
nodes.rationale: Enumerate call sites client-side and resolve callees in batches of 500, instead of one whole-program scan per callable. 4.1 s against a projected 121.9 s, a strict superset of edges, and it needs no callable-classification heuristic because the call site tells you.

nodes.label: Checker.getSignatureUsage
nodes.rationale: The call-graph primitive: resolves through barrels and renamed re-exports and distinguishes an invocation from a reference. It costs 12.6 ms per call at 3,000 files and cannot be batched — passing an array throws.

nodes.label: Trap: getSignatureUsage wants the VariableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: `const f = () => {}` is the dominant callable shape; passing the ArrowFunction or its name Identifier returns 0 usages with no error, so an implementation gets an empty call graph for most of a modern codebase and no indication anything is wrong.

nodes.label: Trap: NodeHandle.path is case-normalised
nodes.rationale: NodeHandle.path is lowercased on macOS while getSourceFileNames() preserves casing, which surfaced as an apparent 0-of-13 edge disagreement. Path normalisation belongs in the adapter, at the boundary, once.

nodes.label: Method dispatch over-approximated across implementations
nodes.rationale: Callers of one implementation include the callers of every sibling, so method edges through a shared name are inferred rather than deterministic and the model must carry provenance per edge instance. The sweep fixes this by resolving to the declared target.

nodes.label: A repository's call graph is a quarter of its call sites
nodes.rationale: 81,888 call sites resolved to repo symbols against 251,648 unattributed, overwhelmingly calls into node_modules. Deduplicated the ratio barely moves, 24.6% to 22.5%, so what trace and impact claim about completeness must be honest about the other three quarters.
nodes.norm_label: a repository's call graph is a quarter of its call sites

nodes.label: The required facts (R/S/L/P/Q ids)
nodes.rationale: Extracted verbatim from PRD §6 and §7 and given ids so the matrix reads compactly; every claim is tagged RUN, SRC or DOC, and nothing rests on a blog post or recollection.

nodes.label: Candidate B: TypeScript 7 unstable/sync API
nodes.rationale: Cross-file type-resolved call attribution works, but there is no call hierarchy, no getImplementationAtPosition and no navigation tree, find-references was not demonstrated, and Microsoft says 7.0 'does not ship with an API' and 7.1 will bring a different one.

nodes.label: Candidate A: TypeScript 6 language service
nodes.rationale: The only candidate shipping LSP-level aggregates as callable functions — findReferences, call hierarchy, getImplementationAtPosition — in-process and stable, at the cost of pre-native speed and a sunset trajectory.

nodes.label: Syntactic candidates: oxc, ast-grep, tree-sitter
nodes.rationale: No type checker and no cross-file resolution, so they are the cheap outer loop and never the symbol graph. Oxc embedding typescript-go as oxlint-tsgolint is the strongest external endorsement of 'fast syntactic layer plus tsgo for types'.

nodes.label: Nothing produces a whole-program call graph
nodes.rationale: Every candidate that resolves a call correctly does so one symbol at a time, so codedocs must drive a per-symbol API across every symbol and assemble the result. PRD §24 should be read as constraining the analysis, not the aggregation.
nodes.norm_label: nothing produces a whole-program call graph

nodes.label: The recommended combination and adapter pipeline
nodes.rationale: Type layer plus a syntactic oxc sweep plus manifests plus git, all behind one adapter into the codedocs model. scip-typescript is not in the pipeline but SCIP is: adopt SCIP-shaped symbol identifiers, keeping the door open to emitting a SCIP index later.
nodes.norm_label: the recommended combination and adapter pipeline

nodes.label: Graphify cannot sit on the deterministic path
nodes.rationale: Its highest-value call edges are the LLM's job and its TS resolution is type-blind name heuristics, so it fails the no-LLM constraint. It stays a sibling tool for documents and rationale — a concept graph over a corpus, not a symbol graph over a program.
nodes.norm_label: graphify cannot sit on the deterministic path

nodes.label: Subprocess versus library obligations
nodes.rationale: Permission is identical; obligations are not. A user-installed subprocess distributes nothing so neither Apache §4 nor the MIT notice clause triggers; shipping a compiled binary is distribution in Object form with no separate-process exemption.

nodes.label: Graphify's mid-life relicensing
nodes.rationale: MIT at 0.8.37 and Apache-2.0 at 0.9.53 under a new GitHub org. Marked AMBIGUOUS on governance, not on the current licence: a single-maintainer project that has relicensed once can relicense again, and a paid one-time-purchase product would be stranded.

nodes.label: psycopg LGPL-3.0-only, disqualified as bundled
nodes.rationale: The single copyleft hit across every tree examined, reachable only through the graphifyy[postgres] extra. LGPL-3.0 §4's relinking and installation-information rules are painful for a bundled commercial CLI, so the extra is never enabled.

nodes.label: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES obligations
nodes.rationale: Full licence text per distinct licence, per-package copyright lines including each tree-sitter grammar separately, verbatim NOTICE contents for every bundled Apache-2.0 package, Oxc's THIRD-PARTY-LICENSE, and a dual-licence election for Biome.

nodes.label: Licence re-verification process
nodes.rationale: Licences are not stable facts — Graphify is the live counter-example. Re-verify on every bump, record the SPDX id and licence-file SHA beside the pinned version, fail the build outside an allowlist, and archive licence files at the pinned version.

nodes.label: Project multiplicity inflated the spike's edge count
nodes.rationale: The spike held `seen` outside the project loop for symbols and inside it for edges, so a file contributed its call sites once per project. 2,874 of 4,827 cal.com files belong to more than one project, a 3.545x multiplicity that tracks the 3.554x over-count.
nodes.norm_label: project multiplicity inflated the spike's edge count

nodes.label: Canonical project per file
nodes.rationale: Restricting the sweep to each file's canonical project costs exactly 2 edges out of 23,039, both a dayjs ambient declaration only some projects include — recorded rather than fixed, and the shape to watch if ambient declarations carry more surface.

nodes.label: Nearest callable ancestor attribution
nodes.rationale: All 5,905 differing edges are the skeleton crediting a strict ancestor of the node the spike credited, with zero unrelated cases: the spike stops at the nearest named ancestor, the skeleton at the nearest callable one.

nodes.label: 6,746 declarations collapse onto 1,571 ids
nodes.rationale: An anonymous callback contributes no segment to a qualified name, so two locals in sibling `it(...)` blocks are indistinguishable; the worst id carries 69 declarations. Bounded to non-durable locals in test files, but a callers answer for such an id over-reports.

nodes.label: The signature-gated incremental wave
nodes.rationale: Tell the compiler the file changed, re-extract that file, and propagate to direct importers only when its export-shape hash moved. 1-3 files and 3-5 ms against 535 ms cold; the naive transitive closure touches 1,435 files and 261 ms for the same edit.

nodes.label: Export-shape hash
nodes.rationale: Computed from typeToString, expanding Interface, TypeAlias, Class and Enum via getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol plus getPropertiesOfType. The gate is the whole game: without it an edit at the base of the graph costs half a rebuild.

nodes.label: Trap: type ids are not stable
nodes.rationale: Type ids are assigned lazily per snapshot, so an id-based shape hash cascades forever — 10 waves and 1,436 of 3,000 files against 1 wave and 1 file. It hides in small tests because ids are stable for files that were not re-checked.
nodes.norm_label: trap: type ids are not stable

nodes.label: Trap: getTypeOfSymbol alone misses interface changes
nodes.rationale: Interfaces report `any` from getTypeOfSymbol and named types print as their own name, so adding a member is invisible to the hash. This is a silent-wrong-answer bug, not a performance issue.
nodes.norm_label: trap: gettypeofsymbol alone misses interface changes

nodes.label: Trap: batching is not optional
nodes.rationale: The API is IPC: 518 ms unbatched against 31 ms with array overloads, a 17x difference that decides whether TS 7 beats TS 6 for bulk traversal. Any adapter must be written array-first, because retrofitting means rewriting the traversal.

nodes.label: .tsbuildinfo as corroboration, not a dependency
nodes.rationale: referencedMap is the import graph and `signature` is the shape hash, so TypeScript's own builder uses precisely this strategy. But the format is undocumented, changed between 6.0.3 and 7.0.2, and only exists for builds that emit.

nodes.label: Cache-key discipline from Nx, Turborepo, Bazel and Rush
nodes.rationale: Adopt content hash plus dependency-graph cascade and hash the tool version and resolved compiler options into the key; reject their task/package/action granularity, because a symbol graph needs file and symbol granularity.
nodes.norm_label: cache-key discipline from nx, turborepo, bazel and rush

nodes.label: What a syntactic tool loses on a barrel file
nodes.rationale: On a 300-statement barrel the syntactic view sees 0 named symbols where the checker sees 601, all declared elsewhere. Barrels are the standard package entry point, so this is the common case, not an edge case.
nodes.norm_label: what a syntactic tool loses on a barrel file

nodes.label: Adopt the SCIP symbol grammar as SymbolId
nodes.rationale: An open, Apache-2.0, versioned specification that already solves fully-qualified cross-package naming for TypeScript, with the containment chain already encoded in the id. Do not invent a symbol ID format.
nodes.norm_label: adopt the scip symbol grammar as symbolid

nodes.label: Transmission format is not a storage format
nodes.rationale: SCIP's own design doc names efficient code navigation a non-goal, and Kythe draws the same line. Naming scheme and store schema are orthogonal layers the PRD conflates; Glean and Sourcegraph each adopted a wire format and built a store.
nodes.norm_label: transmission format is not a storage format

nodes.label: Nobody has solved cross-commit symbol identity
nodes.rationale: SCIP, LSIF, Kythe, Glean and CodeQL all break on rename, move and extract, and stack graphs have no persistent identity at all. Stable identity is not derivable from one snapshot; every system correctly refused to put a heuristic inside a primary key.
nodes.norm_label: nobody has solved cross-commit symbol identity

nodes.label: Version-in-the-ID is wrong for a single-repo tool
nodes.rationale: Sourcegraph indexes many repos at many versions; codedocs indexes one working tree at one commit, where a routine version bump would silently invalidate every symbol in a package and every cross-package reference to it.
nodes.norm_label: version-in-the-id is wrong for a single-repo tool

nodes.label: `local N` needs a path prefix and a non-durable flag
nodes.rationale: Locals are document-scoped and traversal-ordinal. Glean's published fix — prefix the document path — solves uniqueness but not ordinal instability, so codedocs does both and excludes locals from anything that must survive an edit.
nodes.norm_label: `local n` needs a path prefix and a non-durable flag

nodes.label: Steal stack-graphs' storage contract
nodes.rationale: SQLite, per-file rows keyed by path, a content tag, skip on tag match, force flag. It is the only surveyed system with real file-level incrementality, and the contract is independent of the analysis being stack graphs — which are archived.

nodes.label: CodeQL is licence-blocked
nodes.rationale: The CLI terms prohibit use with any codebase that is not an Open Source Codebase, and prohibit database generation for automated analysis or CI. The trap is that the queries are MIT and the CLI is not.

nodes.label: The thirteen operations
nodes.rationale: analyse, symbol, callers, callees, references, file, trace, evidence, docs check, docs affected, impact, doctor and report-bug. Every question repairs the index before it answers, so analyse exists only so a cold build in CI can be a step that fails on its own.

nodes.label: One envelope, every answer
nodes.rationale: Only `result` differs between operations and a failure carries `error` instead, so a parser never meets a second shape. --json is explicit and unbounded, never sniffed from a TTY, because a capped answer an agent reads as whole is a wrong answer with a footnote.

nodes.label: Documents, claims and the four verdicts
nodes.rationale: A claim in an HTML comment is how a file opts in, with no configuration and no docs/** convention. contradicted requires falsification, never mere unresolution, and a blind spot can only turn a would-be contradicted into unable-to-verify, never a verified into one.
nodes.norm_label: documents, claims and the four verdicts

nodes.label: The label layer and the scope channel
nodes.rationale: Two orthogonal axes, role and authorship, because a single exclusive enum drops real source out of the graph — next.config.ts is config and typed source. Every firing signal is stored with its provenance; precedence decides only which one an answer acts on.
nodes.norm_label: the label layer and the scope channel

nodes.label: The index at .codedocs/index.db
nodes.rationale: One SQLite file per working tree holding one snapshot, writing its own .gitignore and always safe to delete. Not committed: it is binary so git cannot delta it, and six commits of a hundred rows grew .git by 25 MB. Drift is detected by stat and tree walk, not git status.

nodes.label: codedocs and fallow, in the README
nodes.rationale: fallow reads the repository's text and reports its hygiene; codedocs resolves its symbols and reports relationships and what a change reaches. The line is the shape of the question.
nodes.norm_label: codedocs and fallow, in the readme

nodes.label: The MCP server
nodes.rationale: One tool per operation derived from the same manifest the CLI parser reads, answered by handing an argv to the function codedocs itself calls, so the bytes are the --json bytes by construction. `mcp` is not an operation and owes no envelope.

nodes.label: Fixture: Markdown carrying no claim
nodes.rationale: The scan reads it and it is not a document, demonstrating that writing a claim is how a file opts in.

nodes.label: Fixture: payments document with claims
nodes.rationale: Exercises calls, reaches, a count on implementations, a count on callers, onlyCalledBy and a negated calls claim, plus a preamble section and an uncovered section so the coverage denominator is not quietly reduced.

nodes.label: Configuration
nodes.rationale: codedocs.jsonc: facts about a repository codedocs cannot determine; optional, strict, never preferences.

nodes.label: Node
nodes.rationale: One of five things the index holds: Package, Project, File, Symbol, Document; Repository is the index header, not a node.

nodes.label: Edge
nodes.rationale: One relationship between two nodes, from a closed set of nine kinds; what PRD Section 25 calls a Relationship.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.rationale: What a file is for: source, test or config; test helpers, mocks and fixtures are test.

nodes.label: Authorship
nodes.rationale: Whether a file was written by a person (authored) or produced by a program (generated); orthogonal to Role.

nodes.label: Package
nodes.rationale: A workspace package as its manifest declares it; a package is not a Project.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.rationale: One TypeScript project: a single tsconfig and the files it globs; what fidelity and the environment fingerprint are held against.

nodes.label: Baseline substitution
nodes.rationale: Using an older baseline because the requested commit has none; part of an answer's scope, never a blind spot.

nodes.label: Draft
nodes.rationale: A Markdown file codedocs writes about one subject with candidate claims marked codedocs?:, never prose, never overwriting.

nodes.label: Report
nodes.rationale: What report-bug writes: one reproduced failure, safe to paste by default; the only artefact meant to leave the machine.

nodes.label: Path
nodes.rationale: trace's result unit: one walk outward from a root symbol, grouped by callee, with why it stopped.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.rationale: Everything the index holds about one subject, assembled for someone else to write prose from; what PRD Section 9's explain becomes.

nodes.label: Impact
nodes.rationale: What a change could reach: symbols reached through the index's edges, resolved against a baseline by continuity.

nodes.label: codedocs
nodes.rationale: A local codebase index for TypeScript: every symbol, every call edge, every project, into one SQLite file, answered deterministically with no LLM, API key, network or daemon.

nodes.label: analyse
nodes.rationale: build or refresh the index; reports a cold build, a repair, or nothing; captures a baseline if the tree is clean.

nodes.label: symbol
nodes.rationale: find a symbol by glob against declared and qualified name; no ranking, ever.

nodes.label: callers
nodes.rationale: every call edge into a subject, followed through barrel files and renamed re-exports.

nodes.label: callees
nodes.rationale: every call edge out of a subject.

nodes.label: references
nodes.rationale: everything that names a subject without calling it: extends, implements, typeReferences, references.

nodes.label: file
nodes.rationale: what the index holds about one file, without guessing a symbol name first.

nodes.label: trace
nodes.rationale: walks outward from a root and returns paths, drawn as a tree with shared prefixes collapsed.

nodes.label: evidence
nodes.rationale: every kind of fact the index holds about one subject in one answer; generates no prose.

nodes.label: impact
nodes.rationale: a walk inward through call and reference edges from symbols a working tree edited, compared against a baseline.

nodes.label: docs check
nodes.rationale: which documented claims the code now contradicts, against four verdicts.

nodes.label: docs affected
nodes.rationale: which documents a change reaches; needs no baseline; never exits 1.

nodes.label: docs draft
nodes.rationale: a Markdown draft of one subject, prefilled with facts as codedocs?: candidate claims.

nodes.label: doctor
nodes.rationale: every unmet precondition and the command that would clear it; static and instant.

nodes.label: report-bug
nodes.rationale: reproduces a failing command and writes one file safe to paste in public unread.

nodes.label: fallow
nodes.rationale: Static analysis tool that reads a repository's text and reports hygiene: dead code, duplication, complexity, architecture boundary violations. codedocs implements no analysis fallow already ships.

nodes.label: cal.com / vscode fixture repositories
nodes.rationale: Fixture repositories cloned into repos/ used to measure codedocs performance claims.

nodes.label: bench/ (fix benchmark)
nodes.rationale: Whether an agent holding codedocs reaches the same fix for less; read as a second measurement, not the product's validation criterion.

nodes.label: Difficulty level
nodes.rationale: How much of the repository an agent must understand to answer, from 1 to 4; excludes lines changed and files touched as signals on purpose.

nodes.label: Level 1 (local)
nodes.rationale: the report points at the code; one file, one project, cause inside or one hop from what the report named; the benchmark's control.

nodes.label: Level 2 (one subsystem, no address)
nodes.rationale: one file, one project, but nothing in the report names it; a lookup plus a local traversal.

nodes.label: Level 3 (across layers)
nodes.rationale: answer spans files in different projects/layers via an interface, service or event rather than a direct call.

nodes.label: Level 4 (a relationship, not a location)
nodes.rationale: cause is not a place but a relationship over time: ownership, ordering, a lifecycle transition; report has no identifier.

nodes.label: The fix benchmark
nodes.rationale: Whether codedocs lets an agent reach the same fix while reading less of the repository; measures cost (tokens, tool calls, files, lines, time), not whether the agent is smarter.

nodes.label: GitHub issue #21
nodes.rationale: The product's validation criterion: a developer question answered correctly that ripgrep and an editor could not answer at all; deliberately rescoped away from the agent-against-agent framing used by the fix benchmark.

nodes.label: Arm (toolset@model)
nodes.rationale: A toolset paired with a model, e.g. codedocs@haiku-4-5; the model belongs to the arm because the benchmark also asks whether structural facts let a cheaper model do work a dearer one otherwise needs.

nodes.label: baseline arm
nodes.rationale: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, TodoWrite, Edit, Write with no extra prompt and the index ignored.

nodes.label: codedocs arm
nodes.rationale: Same tools as baseline plus ~150 tokens describing the five operations, with an index already built.

nodes.label: reference arm
nodes.rationale: The baseline arm with the most runs behind it; every delta in the report is read against it so every percentage answers the same question.

nodes.label: discarded run
nodes.rationale: A run thrown out (not silently counted) when the baseline reaches for codedocs anyway, the codedocs arm never calls it, or no patch is left; biases surviving codedocs runs toward cases the tool suits.

nodes.label: The index cache
nodes.rationale: An index is a pure function of the tree it describes, so the build happens once per commit into repos/.index-cache/<commit>/ and later runs restore it.

nodes.label: One tree per run
nodes.rationale: Every run gets its own detached git worktree at the case's base commit, created before the agent starts and removed when it ends.

nodes.label: Judging the fix
nodes.rationale: hit cannot tell a correct fix from a plausible edit; a judge model with no tools reads the issue, upstream fix and patch three times, blind to which arm wrote it, and returns correctness and similarity grades.

nodes.label: correctness scale (correct/partial/incorrect)
nodes.rationale: Does the patch fix the reported bug?

nodes.label: similarity scale (same-change/same-mechanism/same-area/unrelated)
nodes.rationale: How close is the patch to the fix the maintainers wrote?

nodes.label: Exploration step
nodes.rationale: One tool call that asked the repository something: a Read, Grep, Glob, or a Bash command that prints a file, searches the tree, or queries codedocs; git log/wc/true are not steps.

nodes.label: Lines of source read (src)
nodes.rationale: What every step returned in non-blank lines; separates 'opened the same file' from 'read far less of it', e.g. case #333085.

nodes.label: What counts as touching a symbol (sym)
nodes.rationale: A ground-truth symbol is touched when its name appears on a changed line, its @@ header, or its nearest declaration; separates landing in the same code from landing in the same file.
nodes.norm_label: what counts as touching a symbol (sym)

nodes.label: like-for-like comparison
nodes.rationale: One model, holding the tool and not holding it; the claim codedocs is sold on.

nodes.label: cross-model comparison
nodes.rationale: A cheaper model holding the tool against a dearer model without it; carries the models' difference as well as the toolset's.

nodes.label: bench/RESULTS.md generated write-up

nodes.label: Draft's derived default path (not stdout)
nodes.rationale: The default is a path rather than stdout because a draft is a file about to be edited, and the edit happens in an editor, not in a pipe. A default of stdout makes the first thing every caller does a shell redirect — the one write codedocs cannot refuse, over a file it cannot see, which is the loss ADR 0013 built the overwrite refusal to prevent. Making the write the default moves that gesture inside the refusal. Stdout-by-default (with --out to write) was considered and rejected for the same reason turned one step further: defaulting to the output that needs a redirect makes the unsafe path the ordinary one.

nodes.label: Draft overwrite refusal
nodes.rationale: The refusal to overwrite an existing file is what makes the derived-path default safe, and there is no flag to bypass it. It was the guard on a flag somebody had to pass to get a write; it is now the guard on what happens when nobody says anything. A --force was considered and rejected: the flag exists to be passed, and the file it destroys is a document someone wrote by hand — deleting it first is a gesture that names its own consequence. Any future softening (a --force, an 'only if unchanged', a silent skip) is a change to the command's default behaviour and reopens ADR 0013.

nodes.label: `codedocs?:` candidate marker
nodes.rationale: A draft writes candidate claims under `<!-- codedocs?: ... -->` rather than the checked `<!-- codedocs: ... -->`. `docs check`'s discovery scan tests for the literal prefix `<!-- codedocs:`, which `<!-- codedocs?:` does not match, so a freshly drafted file has claim coverage of nothing because it is not yet a document. Each `?` a person deletes is one assertion they have read the prose for and are prepared to commit to, so coverage counts exactly those — the measure is not inverted, it is moved to where the judgement is. The marker is a question mark, echoing why the checked-claim marker is an HTML comment: invisible in preview, plain text in a diff, one character to remove, and impossible to remove by accident. A frontmatter list of candidates was rejected for the same reason ADR 0005 rejected claims in frontmatter: the list and the prose drift apart silently.

nodes.label: `docs generate` — deleted by ADR 0006, reversed by ADR 0013
nodes.rationale: ADR 0006 deleted `docs generate` on two grounds: it is codedocs writing a document, which ADR 0005 refuses as an unattended write into a file someone else owns; and a skeleton whose every section carries a claim and no prose would invert the coverage measure, reporting full coverage while nothing was written. ADR 0013 reverses the deletion as `docs draft`, answering the first objection with a write that is asked for by name and refuses to overwrite, and the second with the `codedocs?:` candidate marker that keeps a drafted claim out of claim coverage until a person endorses it. The headings-from-a-`trace` shape ADR 0006 sketched and rejected is rejected again in ADR 0013, because heading depth would then track call depth rather than the document.
nodes.norm_label: `docs generate` — deleted by adr 0006, reversed by adr 0013

nodes.label: `docs draft` operation
nodes.rationale: Writes a Markdown file prefilled with everything the index holds about one symbol or file — facts as prose material plus every claim those facts would support as candidates — and writes no sentence of its own prose. Considered and rejected alternatives include leaving the decision alone (an `evidence --json --claims` recipe, rejected because every agent would invent its own layout) and drafting from a `trace` (rejected because heading depth would track call depth).

hyperedges.label: Running-set selection
hyperedges.description: active.ts names the deliberately narrow running set; cases.ts#loadCases filters the frozen prospects pool down to exactly those ids, refusing to run silently fewer cases than declared.

hyperedges.label: Blind judging pipeline
hyperedges.description: judgeRun tops up cached readings via judgeOnce (a no-tools, blinded model call), and judgementFrom/consensus fold multiple readings into one grade per axis (correctness, similarity) with an agreement figure — never a single unverified opinion.

hyperedges.label: Index lifecycle and continuity model
hyperedges.description: An Index describes one Snapshot; Capture copies a finished Index into a Baseline for later comparison; Continuity later resolves a subject across Snapshots/Baselines without ever mutating the live Index.

hyperedges.label: pre-run setup pipeline
hyperedges.description: The three things that must happen before a bench run spends any quota: preflight refuses cases whose declared base commit would void their ground truth, prewarm builds and caches the codedocs index for every commit the surviving cases need, and buildPrompt assembles the task each arm is actually given — all three operate on the same BenchCase[] before any agent is spawned.

hyperedges.label: quota-free reconstruction pipeline
hyperedges.description: recordFrom is a pure fold from a run's saved stream/patch to a RunRecord; rescore.ts replays it over every saved run on disk when scoring logic changes, and rejudge.ts fills in judgements for records rescore left alone — together they let bench/report.ts's numbers be corrected after the fact without re-running the agent.

hyperedges.label: graduated difficulty corpus
hyperedges.description: The prospect pool is built to span the difficulty scale end to end: 333230 is the level-1 control where the file is already named on eight stack frames, 332885 is a level-3 case whose answer crosses two layers joined only through an interface, and 329074 is the level-4 case with the pool's furthest symptom-to-cause distance — together they let bench/report.ts's level grouping show whether codedocs' benefit actually grows with structural distance.

hyperedges.label: single-run pipeline
hyperedges.description: One (case, arm, replicate) cell flows through worktree execution, stream parsing into metrics, diff scoring against ground truth, and judge grading before being filed as a RunRecord — the full measurement pipeline for one benchmark run.

hyperedges.label: blinded two-axis judging
hyperedges.description: The judge is deliberately shown only issue/fix/patch (no arm identity) and graded on two independent axes — correctness and similarity to the maintainers' fix — so resemblance cannot masquerade as correctness.

hyperedges.label: difficulty ladder
hyperedges.description: Four case levels form a structural-complexity ladder from 'report names the file' (level 1, the control) to 'cause is a relationship over time with no identifier' (level 4), testing the claim that codedocs' benefit grows with complexity.

hyperedges.label: The `docs draft` ADR triangle
hyperedges.description: ADR 0013 reverses ADR 0006's deletion of `docs generate` by answering the coverage-inversion objection ADR 0005's claim model raises, via the `codedocs?:` candidate marker; the three ADRs jointly define what `docs draft` may write and why a draft is not a document.

hyperedges.label: Draft write-and-refuse flow
hyperedges.description: main.ts#drafted resolves the target path and calls draft-out.ts#writeDraft; a refusal (draft-exists / draft-unwritable) is rendered back to the user via messages.ts#formatError while the computed draft still reaches stdout, so nothing is lost by the refusal.

hyperedges.label: Benchmark write-up assembly
hyperedges.description: writeup.ts#build composes the prose functions from writeup-prose.ts (question, provenance, standing, limits, colophon) with the tables from writeup-tables.ts into the single generated RESULTS.md, so no number or caveat in the document can exist without a corresponding record on disk.

hyperedges.label: docs draft assembly pipeline
hyperedges.description: draft() owns section selection and bounding; it reads facts through the same assembleEvidence/fileReport an `evidence`/`file` answer uses, shapes them into fact groups via draft-facts.ts, and hands the whole to draft-markdown.ts#markdownFor for byte-identical rendering. Each stage owns one concern: subject resolution, fact assembly, fact-to-line rendering, and file-to-Markdown rendering.

hyperedges.label: candidate/claim consistency guarantee
hyperedges.description: ADR 0013's core promise — a draft cannot disagree with an evidence answer about the same subject — rests on symbolBody and fileBody both calling the same claimsFor() over the same report shapes that evidence() calls it over, rather than each implementing its own restatement.

hyperedges.label: draft file safety contract
hyperedges.description: The manifest declares --out with no --force; the envelope's closed error set enforces refusal to overwrite (draft-exists) and surfaces write failures (draft-unwritable); the candidate marker ensures the file that could be overwritten is never mistaken for a checked document.
